🖌 Happy Rocket Forces and Artillery Day! On the morning of November 19, 1942, preparation fire marked the beginning of the offensive near Stalingrad, which became the turning point of the entire Second World War. Later, this date was chosen as the holiday for Rocket Forces and Artillery Day. Modern high-intensity conflicts cannot do without this branch of the military. Even with the emergence of numerous strike UAVs, artillery has not gone anywhere — let alone rocket systems. During the SMO, gun crews, MLRS systems, and operational-tactical missile systems completed a colossal volume of tasks. And significant changes in tactics of employment and other areas greatly increased the effectiveness of fire strikes compared to what it was at the very beginning. So we wish the artillerymen and rocketeers many new barrels, ammunition in abundance, and keen "eyes" in the sky. And, of course, supplies of the latest systems with enhanced characteristics and capabilities.
